newsitem.title: SPAIN: Unisource calls on Spain to open telecoms market.
newsitem.headline: Unisource calls on Spain to open telecoms market.

text.p: The board of the Unisource telecommunications alliance on Thursday appealed to the Spanish government to open up its telecommunications market as soon as possible so that it can receive European Union approval.

"If the Spanish telecommunications market is not liberalised, the Unisource operation won't be approved," Lars Berg, chairman of the European group, told reporters in Madrid after a board meeting here.
The European Commission has said it will only approve the Unisource alliance if Spain effectively opens up its telecoms market by January 1, 1998, waiving a five-year delay.
Unisource groups telecoms operators Dutch PTT, Telia AB of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT. Telefonica already has 25 percent of the alliance.
Once it is authorised, Unisource wants to conclude a joint venture with U.S. group AT&T to offer its service on a global and not just European level.
"I can't emphasise enough how important the Spanish government's collaboration is (in this matter)," Berg said.
Brussels was expected to make a decision ahead of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting in Singapore in December.
Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga said the Spanish company's shares would suffer if its participation in Unisource was not authorised.
"The non-integration would have a negative impact of between 15 and 20 percent on the share price of Telefonica," he said.
